http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/04/sri-l.text: Sri Lanka closed schools in its tea-growing mountainous regions on Tuesday as heavy rains triggered floods and mudslides that left five people dead and three wounded, officials said.Heavy downpours over the last two days have wreaked havoc in many parts of the country, flooding homes, fields and roads.The mountainous areas in the country’s central region are the worst affected by the severe weather, according to the government’s Disaster Management Centre.So far, five people have died after being buried in mudslides that overran two houses in the central region, while three others were wounded and two people have gone missing, said Pradeep Kodippili, the centre's spokesperson.Kodippili said rains and floods damaged 129 houses and that nearly 2,000 people were evacuated.Navy and army troops have been deployed to rescue people trapped in the floods and help them move to safe places.Local television channel Hiru TV showed troops and civilians rescuing people trapped in their homes because of the floods and facing the risk of being buried by mudflows.Local channels also showed huge rocks, mudslides and fallen electric posts on several main roads in the central region, blocking traffic in some parts of the area.The latest disaster comes as the country is still trying to recover from the devastation in November caused by Cyclone Ditwa that killed nearly 640 people, affected 2 million people and caused an estimated $4.1 billion (€3.5 billion) in damage.The Central province was the hardest hit by that cyclone and the government is struggling to rebuild roads, railways and houses in the region.Mudslides and floods are among the most destructive natural disasters, causing severe damage to lives and property in Sri Lanka every year.Heavy monsoon rains mostly trigger mudslides in the central hill region while flooding low-lying areas, forcing thousands of people to evacuate their homes.

Photograph: Jeff Overs/PA View image in fullscreen Kelin’s name no longer appears on the ‘diplomatic list’ section of the website of the Russian embassy to the UK. Photograph: Jeff Overs/PA Russia Russia withdraws ambassador to UK as Kremlin ratchets pressure over Ukraine support Andrey Kelin left last month after seven years in diplomatic post with no sign yet of anyone replacing him in role Ben Quinn Political correspondent Sun 23 Aug 2026 06.37 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 07.22 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia has withdrawn its ambassador to the UK, it has emerged, as the Kremlin continues to try to put pressure on Britain over its support for Ukraine . Andrey Kelin left last month after seven years in the diplomatic post, with no indication about whether he would be replaced. Tensions have since ratcheted up, with a warning from the Russian embassy last week of “consequences” after it emerged Britain was supplying attack drones to Kyiv. Kelin’s name no longer appears on the “diplomatic list” section of the website of the Russian embassy to the UK. The list of “senior diplomatic staff” now includes only Vasily A Tsyganov, chargé d’affaires at the embassy A gap between ambassadors was not unprecedented, said John Foreman, a former British defence attache in Moscow and Kyiv. But he said in a post on X: “The embassy’s strident ‘consequences’ statement this week and the huge deterioration of bilateral relations since 2018 and especially since the start of the war make me wonder if Moscow will permanently downgrade the relationship this time, by default by not replacing him.” A spokesperson for the Russian embassy told the Sunday Times Kelin had made efforts to preserve channels of communication with the UK and accused the government of choosing a “path of confrontation” with Russia. “He left Britain in the hope that a more constructive and respectful dialogue could eventually be restored, should the UK reconsider its policies towards our country,” he said, adding the Kremlin had not yet put forward a replacement candidate. ​A spokesperson for Britain’s Foreign Office said: “This is a matter for the Russian ministry of foreign affairs. We have an ambassador and embassy in Moscow to engage and raise concerns with the Russian government. “We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine, which has the right to defend itself against Russia’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.” Shaun Pinner, a former British soldier who later fought alongside Ukrainian marines before he was captured and held for a time by Russian forces, said there would be arguments that Kelin’s exit had been a “dangerous erosion” of communication between Britain and Russia but he added that this had not been the case for some time in reality. He said: “If Moscow refuses to meaningfully engage, rebuffs attempts at communication and uses its diplomatic presence primarily to repeat Kremlin narratives, then we shouldn’t pretend we’re witnessing some functioning diplomatic relationship.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Kelin has repeated Kremlin narratives in interviews to British media in recent years. In one on Sky News in June, he said that Russia “cannot lose” the war in Ukraine. He joined the Soviet diplomatic service in 1979. Russia stepped up its rhetoric towards the UK last week after Ministry of Defence sources indicated a report that two drones made by British companies had been used by Ukraine’s military to attack targets inside Russia was true. The Russian embassy, seeking to maximise the impact of its remarks, added in a widely reported statement on Telegram: “London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer.” Explore more on these topics Russia Vladimir Putin Ukraine Europe Foreign policy news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Holding election in wartime would risk destroying Ukraine, says Zelenskyy As Russian missiles rain down on Kyiv, casualties mount and the mood darkens More than 16 killed as Kyiv comes under intense Russian bombardment Volodymyr Zelenskyy sacks senior aide amid Ukraine corruption crisis Sacking turns former Zelenskyy loyalist into potent political opponent Ukraine’s dismissed defence minister calls for wartime presidential election ‘Our task is to laugh at these enemies’: the Ukrainian unit posting drone videos of Russian soldiers’ last moments Moscow threat of ‘consequences’ will not alter UK support for Ukraine, says Burnham Finland halts deportation of Russian family who ‘risked everything’ to oppose Ukraine invasion Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c62jdy.text: Watch: Pupils return to West Bank school behind barbed wire to protect against settlers Watch: Pupils return to West Bank school behind barbed wire to protect against settlers Close A school in the occupied West Bank has been surrounded by barbed-wire fencing as Palestinian parents fear for their children's safety due to the rise of Israeli settler attacks in the area. The isolated village of al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, has been increasingly surrounded by Jewish settler outposts, and regularly blocked by Israeli forces who frequently operate an ad-hoc checkpoint at the entrance. Six people, including three pupils at the school, have been killed in al-Mughayyir this year, in a surge of settler-related violence against Palestinians. One of them, 14-year-old Aws al-Naasan, was shot dead by a settler outside the school gates in April. All Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. Many of the small ad-hoc settler outposts that have mushroomed around al-Mughayyir are illegal under Israeli law too. Read more on this story. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Isle Royale, Michigan, a national park in the middle of Lake Superior. Photograph: Per Breiehagen/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Isle Royale, Michigan, a national park in the middle of Lake Superior. Photograph: Per Breiehagen/Getty Images Michigan Missing US hiker, 70, found injured on remote island after week-long search Craig Berg was hypothermic but alert when located on Isle Royale by Michigan police and officials during solo hike Keely Aouga Sun 13 Sep 2026 19.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 70-year-old hiker who had been missing for a week on a Michigan island was rescued on Saturday, according to the US Coast Guard. Craig Berg was located on Isle Royale with the help of backpackers, Michigan state police troopers and local officials. Even though Berg was found injured and hypothermic, he is “alive and alert”, according to a statement posted to the Isle Royale national park’s Facebook page . After Berg was located, a MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from US Coast Guard Air Station Traverse City hoisted Berg from the island and transported him to Marquette regional airport in Gwinn, Michigan , 140 miles (230km) away. The Isle Royale national park’s statement reported that Berg had been missing since 5 September. Berg was on what was planned as a nine-day solo backpacking hike on the large Lake Superior island. He was supposed to take a ferry back to Michigan’s Upper Peninsula on 5 September, but family members said that he did not arrive home. According to Local 4 , a Detroit station, Berg’s family reported him missing when the hiker did not return as planned. Search and rescue missions began on 6 September. Crews first focused on Rock Harbor, where Berg planned to end his hike, then expanded to other areas – including the Greenstone Ridge trail, where a trail camera captured Berg on 30 August, the report added. In an interview with TV6 , Berg’s son, Evan, said that he is happy and relieved that his father has been located. “He was in rough shape, but he’s okay,” Evan said. “He’s able to speak. He asked for food and water. We’re just so grateful, and we couldn’t be more happy and relieved, and we appreciate all the support we’ve had on social media, and we are just so grateful.” The National Park Service thanks the employees and partners who helped during the search. ​Isle Royale is a remote national park with no roads or wheeled vehicles allowed. Ground search teams navigating the island’s 200 sq miles of solid land must move strictly by foot through dense boreal forest and rocky ridges. Berg’s rescue brings a successful conclusion to an intensive, week-long multi-agency operation across the remote, roadless island. Photograph: Tracey Nearmy/The Guardian South Australia Man and woman charged after baby boy found dead in Adelaide motel South Australia police say infant was aged between six and seven months old and had been ‘deceased for a period of time’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Tue 13 Oct 2026 03.09 EDT Last modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 03.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man and a woman have been charged after a baby boy was found dead in a motel. Benjamin Nicholas Houghton, 40, and Yue Ning Lieu, 42, are in custody after police discovered the child during a welfare check at a Glen Osmond motel in Adelaide’s south on Saturday. “The infant had been deceased for a period of time,” South Australia police said in a statement on Tuesday. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email A post-mortem confirmed the boy was aged between six and seven months old, police said. The man and woman had been living at the Tollgate Motel since they arrived in SA at the start of the year, police said. Houghton and Lieu have been charged with criminal neglect and destroy human remains to pervert the course of justice. Their matters appeared in Adelaide magistrates court on Monday. They did not apply for bail and were remanded in custody until 3 May 2027. SA police’s eastern district detectives conducted the initial investigation. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “However, due to the nature and complexity of the incident and the resources required, Major Crime Investigation Branch have taken over the investigation,” a police statement said. “Police are seeking assistance from anyone who has stayed at the Tollgate Motel, and specifically anyone who has information about the occupants of room four to contact Crime Stoppers.” Explore more on these topics South Australia Adelaide news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Man charged with sexual abuse of children linked to former Adelaide youth detention centre Three boys crawled into a skip bin one night and by morning one was dead. https://www.sthelensstar.co.uk/news/2662.text: Murder Court Crime Whiston Four men jailed for 112 years after fatal petrol attack Murder Court Crime Whiston By Conaill Corner Reporter Share 0 Comments 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. FOUR men have been jailed for a combined 112 years after a father-of-two was kidnapped, doused in petrol and set alight before dying at Whiston Hospital. Tomasz Samel, 45, died at the hospital on June 21, 2019, almost three months after being subjected to a horrific attack linked to the loss of cigarettes worth £1 million. Neil Jones, 49, of no fixed address, and Tobiasz Kozlowski, 38, of Kirkby, Merseyside, were both jailed for life after being convicted of murder. Jones was given a minimum term of 34 years in prison, while Kozlowski received a minimum term of 33 years. Co-defendant Kevin Wooden, 46, of Banbury, Oxfordshire, was sentenced to 23 years in prison, while Kye Arthur, 35, of Lockleaze, Bristol, was jailed for 22 years after both were convicted of manslaughter. (Left to right) Kye Arthur, Neil Jones, Tobias Kozlowski, Kevin Wooden (Image: West Midlands Police) Kozlowski's wife, Sandra Kozlowska, 38, of Kirkby, was given a three-year prison sentence, suspended for three years, after being convicted of assisting an offender. The sentences were handed down at Birmingham Crown Court on Friday, October 9. 'Truly horrific' attack Mr Samel was kidnapped from his home in Raleigh Road, Handsworth, Birmingham, at around 8.35am on March 27, 2019. Wooden and Arthur, alongside a third person who has not been identified, were paid to abduct him. They initially posed as Amazon delivery drivers before claiming to be law enforcement officers. Mr Samel was placed in a white van and driven to Merseyside, where he was detained for several hours. He was eventually stripped naked and, while seated and defenceless, had petrol thrown over him before being set alight. Mr Justice Wall told the defendants: "You all chose to involve yourselves in a truly horrific series of events." The judge said the motive was that Mr Samel had been held responsible for the loss of a consignment of cigarettes worth £1 million, which had been seized by HM Revenue and Customs. He said: "After a number of hours of detention, he was stripped naked, and, while seated and defenceless, petrol was thrown over him and he was set alight. "He suffered extensive burns to most of his body. He was then dressed and driven to a remote area where he was thrown out of a vehicle onto the side of the road." Mr Samel was dumped near Bickerstaffe, close to Rainford where he knocked on the door of a property seeking help at around 11.10pm on the same day. Tomasz Samel, who died in Whiston Hospital after being subjected to torture (Image: West Midlands Police) The judge said descriptions of his injuries given by paramedics and others who saw him were "harrowing and disturbing". He added: "The level of his suffering between the time at which the injuries were inflicted and his death is difficult to imagine." Mr Samel was taken to Whiston Hospital, where he remained for almost three months before dying from his injuries on June 21, 2019. Cigarettes worth £1 million seized The attack was linked to cigarettes which had been illegally imported into the UK from Poland. Mr Samel had been in possession of the consignment at a unit in Aston, Birmingham, when HMRC seized it on February 22, 2019. He was the subject of an international arrest warrant at the time of his kidnapping. The judge described the plot as a "carefully executed plan" and said Kozlowski and Jones were the organisers because they had a financial stake in the cigarettes which were seized. He said he was sure Kozlowski was present when Mr Samel was set alight, although he could not say whether he had "lit the flame". The judge added that other people in Poland or the UK might also have played a role in organising the events. However, he said any involvement by others did not diminish the defendants' responsibility. Jones and Kozlowski pleaded guilty to conspiracy to kidnap and conspiracy to falsely imprison before the trial began. Jones had also admitted manslaughter. Wooden and Arthur admitted conspiracy to kidnap and conspiracy to falsely imprison. A jury unanimously convicted Jones and Kozlowski of murder and conspiracy to cause grievous bodily harm in August, while Wooden and Arthur were convicted of manslaughter. Kozlowska was convicted of helping her husband avoid detection by police. Investigation spanned several countries The investigation involved enquiries in Poland, Greece, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Colombia, France, Scotland and Wales, where members of the gang had operations or had fled after the kidnapping. Kate Seal, of the Crown Prosecution Service, said: "This was a sustained and merciless attack on a man taken from the safety of his own home." Read more Man charged with five counts of possession of a knife Teen due in court after 4 injured as car left road and hit tree Woman accused of stealing whiskey and injuring security worker Ex-Merseyside Police officer jailed for rape and sexual assault She said bringing those responsible to justice required years of work, including co-operation with West Midlands Police and international partners across three countries to gather forensic, digital and witness evidence. Ms Seal added: "Mr Samel's family have shown extraordinary strength throughout this ordeal. "Our thoughts remain with them, and I hope these sentences reflect the severity of what was inflicted on Mr Samel and provide the family with a sense of justice being achieved, though nothing can undo their loss." Hungary: 70 years after Soviet crackdown, leaders honour uprising victims Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 24/10/2026 - 0:07 GMT+2 Seventy years after Hungary's 1956 uprising against Soviet rule, Prime Minister Péter Magyar paid tribute to its victims as Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the importance of freedom and democracy. … More Prime Minister Péter Magyar attended a flag-raising ceremony outside parliament on Lajos Kossuth Square before laying flowers at memorials and graves, including that of Imre Nagy , the former prime minister executed after the 1956 revolution . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The uprising, which began on 23 October 1956 , lasted 15 days before Soviet troops and tanks crushed the revolt , killing up to 3,000 revolutionaries . European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen joined the commemorations, addressing Hungarian lawmakers during a special parliamentary session attended by European Council President António Costa . She praised the courage of Hungarians who fought for freedom, democracy, and justice , drawing parallels with the country's recent political transition following Viktor Orbán's departure from power. Her visit comes as Budapest seeks the release of billions of euros in frozen EU funding , withheld over rule-of-law and corruption concerns. Brussels maintains that further reforms are needed before the funds can be unlocked, a key challenge for Magyar's new government.
